stories.headline: Nvidia pitches Vera CPUs to Chinese customers with orders open and August availability

key_facts.fact: Nvidia told Chinese clients its Vera CPU for AI data centers could be available as soon as August and that they can begin placing orders.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has informed Chinese customers that Vera CPUs for AI data centers could be available as early as August, and is already inviting orders, according to three sources.

key_facts.fact: One major Chinese cloud provider is preparing an initial order of more than 300 dual-Vera-CPU servers, planned for testing in overseas data centers first.
key_facts.excerpt: One major Chinese cloud provider is preparing to order more than 300 servers configured with two Vera CPUs each. The company intends to first use these systems for testing... One of the sources said Chinese customers plan to initially deploy Vera chips only in their overseas data centers for testing.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is targeting roughly $20 billion in Vera revenue by the end of its fiscal year to end-January, with single-CPU prices well north of $20,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Target Vera revenue | $20 billion by end of fiscal year to end-January... Estimated single Vera CPU price | 'Well north' of $20,000 (before bulk discounts)

key_facts.fact: Vera is Nvidia's first standalone CPU, designed for agentic AI, and positions the Arm-based chip against Intel and AMD in the server CPU market.
key_facts.excerpt: The sources noted that some Chinese clients have expressed interest in the Vera chip, Nvidia's first standalone central processing unit designed for agentic AI—systems that perform tasks autonomously... Nvidia claims it runs up to 1.8 times faster than comparable processors from rivals.

key_facts.fact: The pitch comes after Nvidia's market share in China effectively dropped to zero amid US export controls on advanced AI chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's market share in China has effectively dropped to zero, as stated by its CEO Jensen Huang in October, due to U.S. export controls on advanced chips and China's push for self-reliance in key technologies.

stories.headline: Google taps Samsung for Icefish TPU memory I/O die as TSMC capacity tightens

key_facts.fact: Google is in talks to outsource production of the memory input/output die for its 10th-generation TPU, codenamed Icefish, to Samsung's 2-nanometer foundry process.
key_facts.excerpt: Google is in talks to outsource production of the memory I/O Die — a key component connecting the computing unit and HBM in the 10th-generation TPU (code-named Ice Fish) — to Samsung Electronics' 2-nanometer process.

key_facts.fact: TSMC will continue to manufacture the TPU's core computing engine, expected to use its 1.4-nanometer process.
key_facts.excerpt: Google plans to produce the core computing chip at TSMC's 1.4-nanometer process, while Samsung is expected to manufacture the memory input/output die (I/O Die)—a critical component connecting the core chip with high-bandwidth memory (HBM)—using its 2-nanometer process.

key_facts.fact: The split-foundry strategy reflects TSMC's saturated capacity for AI chips and Google's desire to lock in Samsung HBM supply.
key_facts.excerpt: As TSMC's supply chain bottleneck deepens, Google has turned its attention to Samsung Electronics' 'comprehensive semiconductor solution,' which encompasses HBM, advanced processes, and packaging capabilities... Some analysts also suggest that Google is seeking to secure a head start on HBM, which is in short supply, by using foundry orders as leverage.

key_facts.fact: Samsung has supplied more than 60% of the HBM used in Google's TPUs over the past year.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung supplying more than 60% of the HBM for Google's TPUs last year.

key_facts.fact: Icefish is expected to enter mass production as early as 2028, with discussions still in early stages.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The 10th-generation TPU is expected to enter mass production as early as 2028, and current discussions are in their early stages,' a semiconductor industry official said.

key_facts.fact: Google is also reportedly in talks with Intel for some TPU components, in addition to Samsung.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics is expected to take on a portion of the production for Google's next-generation artificial intelligence (AI) chip. Google is also reportedly in negotiations with Intel.

stories.headline: Anthropic signs 12+ data center lease LOIs covering 1+ GW, seeks Google financial guarantee

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has signed more than a dozen preliminary agreements to lease US data centers with combined capacity exceeding 1 gigawatt.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic, the creator of the Claude Code AI assistant, has signed more than a dozen preliminary agreements to lease U.S. data centers with a combined capacity of more than 1 GW, The Information reported, citing sources with direct knowledge of the plans.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic executives discussed having Google provide a financial guarantee on the lease payments, building on Google's role co-designing the server chips Anthropic would use.
key_facts.excerpt: The AI startup's executives have also discussed an arrangement under which backer Google, which co-designs some of the server chips Anthropic could use in the facilities, would provide a financial guarantee for its lease payments.

key_facts.fact: Google declined to comment on the discussions and Anthropic did not immediately respond.
key_facts.excerpt: In an emailed response, Google said it does not comment on rumors or speculation, while Anthropic did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.

key_facts.fact: Apollo Global Management and Blackstone are providing private credit as part of the wider financing structure tied to Anthropic compute.
key_facts.excerpt: Executives at the company have also reportedly discussed an arrangement where Google would financially backstop those lease payments, with Apollo Global Management and Blackstone providing private credit as part of the wider financing structure.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic raised $65 billion in late May at a $965 billion post-money valuation and filed confidentially for a US IPO earlier this month.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic last raised funds in late May, securing $65 billion at a post-money valuation of $965 billion, placing it ahead of OpenAI... Anthropic announced that it had confidentially filed for a U.S. IPO.

key_facts.fact: Google had earlier announced plans to invest up to $40 billion in Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: In April, the AI startup said that Alphabet planned to invest up to $40 billion in Anthropic.

stories.headline: Crusoe pushed out of 1.8 GW Wyoming Project Jade campus after Google raised cost concerns

key_facts.fact: Crusoe paused development on Project Jade, a planned 1.8 GW data center campus in Cheyenne, Wyoming, that was designed to scale up to 10 GW.
key_facts.excerpt: Crusoe has paused work on Project Jade, a massive campus planned for Cheyenne, Wyoming. The 1.8GW facility was announced last year, with claims it could scale to 10GW.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported that Google, the prospective customer, raised concerns about costs and the construction timetable and pressured Crusoe to step aside.
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg reported that Google raised concerns about costs and the construction timetable under Crusoe's management, and the company was pressured to leave. A Crusoe spokesperson told Bloomberg the company did not have a signed agreement with the prospective customer but had entered into exclusive talks.

key_facts.fact: Tallgrass Energy, the Blackstone-backed utility partner, will continue the project and is working directly with the prospective customer.
key_facts.excerpt: Black Hills, the utility partner on the project, said it is continuing without Crusoe and working directly with the prospective large-load customer, with service tracking for early 2028.

key_facts.fact: Crusoe says it now has 4.9 GW of data center capacity under contract for Crusoe Cloud and a development pipeline exceeding 40 GW.
key_facts.excerpt: Crusoe said that it has contracted 4.9GW of data center infrastructure for Crusoe Cloud. It claimed that its total development pipeline – including contracted projects, sites under active tenant negotiation, and sites in advanced development – exceeds 40GW.

key_facts.fact: Crusoe's flagship Abilene, Texas site lost Oracle and OpenAI to delays before Microsoft picked up the remaining capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Its flagship site in Abilene, Texas, was developed for Oracle and OpenAI but saw the customers pull out of the later stages due to delays. Microsoft ultimately picked up the remaining capacity at the site.

stories.headline: KKR launches Helix Digital Infrastructure with $10B+ from Kuwait, Nvidia and Vistra

key_facts.fact: KKR, the Kuwait Investment Authority, Nvidia and Vistra launched Helix Digital Infrastructure with more than $10 billion of committed capital to build AI data centers, power and connectivity.
key_facts.excerpt: KKR, together with the Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) and Vistra (NYSE: VST) today announced the launch of Helix Digital Infrastructure ('Helix')... the Helix strategy has more than $10 billion in total long-duration capital commitments to date.

key_facts.fact: Helix will be led by former AWS chief Adam Selipsky, with KKR's global head of digital infrastructure Waldemar Szlezak as chief investment officer.
key_facts.excerpt: The company will be led by former Amazon Web Services CEO Adam Selipsky, while KKR's Global Head of Digital Infrastructure, Waldemar Szlezak, will serve as chief investment officer.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia will be a cornerstone strategic partner, supplying its DSX AI-factory architecture; Vistra will be Helix's preferred power provider.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA will also serve as a strategic partner to support the deployment of NVIDIA DSX AI factory-aligned infrastructure with a view to maximizing tokens per watt, achieving lowest total cost of ownership and accelerating time to first token... Vistra, a leading integrated power generation and electricity company with operations across 18 states and Washington, D.C., will be the preferred power provider for Helix investments.

key_facts.fact: Helix sits inside KKR's infrastructure business, which manages more than $100 billion globally and has invested over $70 billion in digital infrastructure and power.
key_facts.excerpt: The initiative is backed by KKR's infrastructure business, which manages more than $100 billion in infrastructure assets globally and has invested over $70 billion across digital infrastructure and power-related sectors.

key_facts.fact: The launch follows Apollo and Blackstone's recently announced $35 billion private credit program linked to Anthropic projects.
key_facts.excerpt: The launch of Helix is part of a broader trend of private capital mobilization around artificial intelligence infrastructure. The rising cost of data centers and computing capacity is attracting numerous financial players, similar to Apollo and Blackstone, which recently announced a $35bn program linked to Anthropic projects.

stories.headline: Bezos's Prometheus raises $12B Series B at $41B valuation to build an 'artificial general engineer'

key_facts.fact: Prometheus raised $12 billion in Series B funding at a roughly $41 billion valuation, bringing total funding above $18 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Prometheus, the physical AI startup co-founded by Jeff Bezos and Vik Bajaj, the former co-founder of Verily, Google's life sciences unit, announced it raised $12 billion at a $41 billion valuation.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Bezos himself, with JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, DST Global and Arch Venture Partners participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Investors in the round include JPMorgan, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, DST Global and Arch Venture Partners, according to Axios. Bezos was the largest backer of the company's $6.2 billion Series A, and he said in a CNBC interview at the company's San Francisco headquarters that he participated in the new round as well.

key_facts.fact: Prometheus is building what Bezos calls an 'artificial general engineer' to compress the design-to-manufacturing cycle for jet engines, chips, medical devices and other physical products.
key_facts.excerpt: Prometheus is pursuing what Bezos calls an 'artificial general engineer': AI tools capable of compressing the full cycle from design to manufacturing for complex physical systems. The targets include jet engines, medical devices, semiconductors, advanced materials, and consumer electronics.

key_facts.fact: Bezos said much of the new capital will go to compute needs and to building specialized training data.
key_facts.excerpt: 'This is a capital-intensive startup, there's no question about that,' Bezos said, citing the cost of compute and of building the specialized training data the company needs.

key_facts.fact: Prometheus has about 150 employees across San Francisco, London and Zurich, with co-founder Vik Bajaj serving as co-CEO.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, which currently has 150 employees across offices in San Francisco, London, and Zurich, is keeping the specifics of what it has already built under wraps.

key_facts.fact: Bezos addressed reports that he is also seeking up to $100 billion for a related fund to buy manufacturing companies that Prometheus could help optimize.
key_facts.excerpt: Bezos also addressed reports that he is seeking to raise as much as $100 billion for an affiliated fund to buy manufacturing companies. He said Prometheus may buy parts of companies that could benefit from its technology, and help them improve their manufacturing processes.

stories.headline: EngineAI files confidentially for Hong Kong IPO at $1.5B valuation amid China robotics rush

key_facts.fact: Shenzhen-based humanoid robotics startup EngineAI has filed confidentially for an initial public offering in Hong Kong.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese robotics startup EngineAI has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong initial public offering, seeking to tap strong investor demand for robotics and artificial intelligence firms, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: EngineAI is working with China International Capital Corp (CICC) and CITIC Securities on the proposed listing, with size and timing still undetermined.
key_facts.excerpt: The Shenzhen-based company is working with China International Capital Corp (CICC) (HK:3908) and CITIC Securities (HK:6030) on the proposed listing... Details, including the size and timing of the offering, have yet to be determined.

key_facts.fact: EngineAI was valued at more than $1.5 billion after a 200 million yuan ($27.9 million) Series B in April, led by Henan CICC Huirong Fund Management and Luxshare-ICT.
key_facts.excerpt: The confidential filing comes on the heels of a $200 million Series B funding round that valued the company at $1.5 billion. That round was led by Henan CICC Huirong Fund Management and Luxshare-ICT, the latter being a major electronics manufacturer that supplies components for some of the world's biggest consumer tech brands.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2023, EngineAI gained attention last year for a video of its humanoid robot performing a front flip.
key_facts.excerpt: EngineAI, founded in 2023, is among a new generation of Chinese robotics firms aiming to commercialize humanoid robots. The company gained attention last year after releasing a video showing one of its robots performing a frontflip.

key_facts.fact: EngineAI joins a pipeline of Chinese robotics IPO candidates including Unitree Robotics and robotic-hand maker PaXini Tech.
key_facts.excerpt: Several peers, including Unitree Robotics and robotic-hand maker PaXini Tech, are also pursuing listings in Hong Kong or mainland China.
